answer:
The energy levels of a particle in a 1D box of length $L$ are given by:
$$E_n = \frac{n^2 h^2}{8 m L^2}$$

Given data: $L = 30\text{ 	ext{AA}} = 30 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$, $n = 1$ (lowest energy level), mass of electron $m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$, $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$.

$$E_1 = \frac{(1)^2 (6.626 \times 10^{-34})^2}{8 (9.11 \times 10^{-31}) (30 \times 10^{-10})^2}$$
$$E_1 = \frac{4.39 \times 10^{-67}}{6.56 \times 10^{-47}} \approx 6.69 \times 10^{-21}\text{ J} \approx 0.042\text{ eV}$
proTip: Convert the final answer from Joules to electron-volts (eV) as it is standard practice.
